claims.quote: Standard library adds the deterministic proleptic Gregorian UTC `time` module (`time/parse`, `time/fromParts`, `time/format`, `time/parts`, `time/diff`, `time/add`) operating on exact integer UTC epoch milliseconds with zero host-timezone dependency.
`time/parse`, `time/fromParts`, `time/format`, `time/parts`, `time/diff`, and `time/add` normalize timezones, reject impossible dates, round-trip ISO-8601 UTC strings, and compute exact durations.

String module adds Unicode regular expression matching and extraction (`string/matches?`, `string/match`, `string/matchAll` with stateless flags from `i`, `m`, `s` and pure JSON match records) and canonical quote/entity normalization (`string/normalize`).

`string/matches?`, `string/match`, `string/matchAll`, and `string/normalize` extract structured matches and canonicalize typographic quotes, dashes, ellipses, and whitespace inside plain code and Datalog rules.
Proof module adds `proof/facts` and `proof/assumptions` to extract deduplicated, canonically sorted ground (`given: true`) facts and leaf closed-world absences from any `why` explanation tree.
`proof/facts` and `proof/assumptions` compose with `why` across rules, queries, `find`, and `assuming` to derive ground evidence lineage and negative dependencies.

Graph module adds `graph/lca` (lowest common ancestors and shortest hop distances in any DAG), `graph/simplePaths` (all cycle-free directed paths up to `maxHops` with optional weights), and `graph/dominators` (immediate dominator tree rooted at `start`).
`graph/lca`, `graph/simplePaths`, and `graph/dominators` run deterministically over base and derived edge relations.

The `lion` CLI adds `lion diff` to compute deterministic semantic diffs between two saved databases or preview the in-memory impact of `--apply` / `--eval` steps without touching disk, including derived conclusion deltas with `--derived`; `@lionlang/metrics` adds `bun run efficacy [--against <ref>]` to benchmark Lion's efficacy for AI agents building deep research knowledge bases, ontologies, and graphs.
